statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk stays low because the 22:00Z Globex reopen absorbed Intuit's guidance cut without index-level dislocation after an orderly, two-sided 25 August session, while Stress remains elevated ahead of Wednesday's stacked 12:30Z PCE and GDP cluster and the NVIDIA report after the U.S. close.
recommendation: The 25 August cash session closed higher and two-sided: the Nasdaq-100 index finished at 29,209.23, up 0.64% inside a 29,077.72-29,338.77 range, with the S&P 500 up 0.32% at 7,677.28, the Nasdaq Composite up 0.66% at 26,151.30 and the Dow up 0.30% at 53,577.40. NQ futures reopened at 22:00Z near 29,291 against the 29,287.50 settlement inside a range of roughly 25 points, so Intuit's 7.2% after-hours decline on below-consensus fiscal 2027 guidance has so far stayed a single-name event. VIX at 15.45 is 0.40 lower on the day, Treasury yields eased and WTI fell about 3% to a one-week low as U.S.-Iran tension was read as economic rather than military pressure. That combination describes functioning rather than failing mean reversion, so Tail stays at 10 and the mapped state remains EA_ON. A narrow danger window is published for 20:00-21:00Z on 26 August, covering the NVIDIA release into thin post-close futures liquidity; that is the only forecast hour mapped to yellow. Stress at 47 carries the 12:30Z macro cluster and the NVIDIA report, both of which are conditional catalysts rather than observed structure.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures reopen flat as Intuit's guidance cut is absorbed, leaving Tail low into a stacked Wednesday of PCE, GDP and the NVIDIA report
body:
The 25 August U.S. cash session closed higher without any sign of one-way structure. The Nasdaq-100 index settled at 29,209.23, up 186.05 points or 0.64%, inside a 29,077.72-29,338.77 range and comfortably above the session low, while the S&P 500 added 0.32% to 7,677.28, the Nasdaq Composite 0.66% to 26,151.30 and the Dow 0.30% to 53,577.40. The move was a technology rebound rather than a broad melt-up: the semiconductor index recovered 1.4% after Monday's 2.7% decline, AMD gained 4.9% on a broker upgrade, NVIDIA rose about 2.2% and ended its longest losing streak since 2022, and Meta added close to 2%. Megacap participation was split, with four of the eight largest Nasdaq names lower on the day, which is consistent with two-sided rather than persistent directional trade.

The structurally decisive observation for this assessment is the 22:00Z Globex reopen. Intuit reported fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter results ahead of expectations but guided fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS to $22.88-$23.12 against a $27.30 consensus, and its shares fell about 7.2% after hours. NQ futures nevertheless reopened near 29,291 against the 29,287.50 settlement, inside a range of roughly 25 points in the first half hour, so the guidance cut has been priced at the single-name level without transmitting into index-level dislocation.

Cross-assets support rather than amplify that read. VIX closed at 15.45, down 0.40 on the day with a 15.13-16.30 range, which is a contained level and a declining path. The most recent official H.15 column, for 24 August, shows the 2-year at 4.24% and the 10-year at 4.70%, and longer-dated yields eased further on 25 August. WTI fell about 3% to a one-week low after the latest U.S. measures against Iran were read as economic pressure rather than military escalation, with Pakistani mediation in Tehran and continued Qatari diplomacy cited. Canada announced retaliatory tariffs on roughly $20bn of U.S. goods effective 8 September and the index absorbed it. Shared delayed cross-asset context is aligned with this picture, showing Treasury futures firmer, the VIX future about 2.2% lower and crude about 3.1% lower.

The next 24 hours are dominated by two scheduled checkpoints rather than by current structure. At 12:30Z on 26 August the July PCE and core PCE price indices, the second estimate of Q2 GDP, advance durable goods orders and personal income and spending print together, and the U.S. cash open follows an hour later. After the 20:00Z close, NVIDIA reports Q2 FY2027 against consensus near $92bn of revenue and $2.09 of adjusted EPS, with data-centre revenue expected near $85bn. Options positioning has been described as pricing an unusually contained reaction, which is itself a source of gap risk if the outcome differs. The single mechanism capable of denying meaningful mean reversion is a large repricing running through thin post-close futures liquidity, and that is why the only forecast hour mapped to yellow, and the published danger window, is 20:00-21:00Z on 26 August. Event importance, forecast dispersion and surprise magnitude elsewhere in the window are carried by Stress and Confidence, not by Tail.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 hours the assessment stayed inside the low-to-watch Tail band and never approached the block threshold. Tail sat between 8 and 12 through the 24 August U.S. evening and the Asian session under normal and mixed modes, then built steadily from 04:00Z on 25 August as a trend-up bias developed, reaching 15 to 17 by the European morning. Between 09:00Z and 13:00Z the reading held the 20-21 watch band across the European session, the U.S. pre-market and the first cash hour, the only stretch of the window mapped to yellow. From 14:00Z the mode reverted to mixed as the U.S. session produced two-way trade rather than continuation, and Tail decayed steadily from 17 to 11 into the close and the maintenance break. Stress moved in a narrow 42-51 band throughout, tracking the approach of the 26 August calendar rather than any observed failure of mean reversion, and Confidence held between 84 and 88.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours divide into four phases. The first runs from the current 22:00Z Globex reopen through the Asian session, where no U.S. release is scheduled and conditional Tail eases from 10 to a low of 9 on an assumed contained range. The second is the European morning and U.S. pre-market, where conditional Tail rises gradually from 10 to 13 as positioning narrows toward the U.S. data cluster; this is a positioning phase, so no post-event alignment is treated as observed. The third phase is the 12:30Z release cluster and the 13:30Z cash open, where conditional Tail peaks at 17 and then 16 under event/whipsaw modes, covering a two-stage repricing in which an opening auction continues the post-release direction without retracement; conditional Tail then decays through the afternoon to 11 on an assumed orderly price discovery. The fourth phase is the NVIDIA report: conditional Tail rises to 13 in the power hour and to 21 in the 20:00Z hour, the only slot mapped to yellow, because the release lands in thin post-close futures liquidity where a large repricing can run with little two-way flow. The final hour is the 21:00-22:00Z CME maintenance break, in which no price path forms and conditional Tail falls back to 12 while Stress stays at 66, since any second leg is deferred to the following reopen.
